master.definition_en: A parasitic infection caused by tapeworms of the genus Taenia. Humans are infected by eating undercooked or raw meat of infected animals. It is usually an asymptomatic infection and patients may become aware of the infection by noticing segments of the tapeworm in their feces. If symptoms are present, they include nausea, abdominal pain, indigestion, constipation, or diarrhea.

master.definition_en: Infectious disease that is transmitted through the bite of hematophagous female phlebotomine sand flies. The clinical spectrum ranges from asymptomatic to clinically overt disease which can remain localized to the skin or disseminate to the upper oral and respiratory mucous membranes or throughout the reticulo-endothelial system. Three main clinical syndromes have been described: visceral (or Kala-Azar; with fever, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly), cutaneous, and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis (cutaneous or mucocutaneous ulceration).

curated.category: 寄生虫病与热带传染病
curated.lethality_detail_zh: 经白蛉叮咬传播利什曼原虫所致；其中内脏利什曼病（俗称“黑热病”）若未及时规范抗虫治疗，数周至数月内因全血细胞减少、严重继发细菌感染、出血及恶病质致死，未治者病死率超过95%！
curated.treatability_summary_zh: 内脏利什曼病（黑热病）早期使用两性霉素B脂质体、葡萄糖酸锑钠或米替福新规范疗程后绝大多数可彻底治愈，但误诊延误率高且部分患者可能复发。

annual_deaths_global.range_or_note: WHO估算全球每年约70万–100万例各型利什曼病新发病例（其中致命性内脏利什曼病约5万–9万例/年），导致约20,000–30,000例死亡。

annual_deaths_china.range_or_note: 中国以散在山区/荒漠型内脏利什曼病（黑热病）为主，2023年全国共报告299例（较2022年上升25.1%，主要集中于山西、河南、陕西等省及少量输入病例），及时救治后死亡极少。
annual_deaths_china.source: 中国国家传染病报告系统 (NDRIS 2023)

epidemiology.prevalence_global: 全球超10亿人口居住在利什曼病流行区，年新发内脏型5万–9万例、皮肤型60万–100万例。
epidemiology.prevalence_china: 2023年全国报告299例内脏利什曼病，集中于晋豫陕交界丘陵山区（如山西114例、河南54例、陕西38例）及新疆荒漠区，呈局部回升态势。

clinical_management.acute_emergency_protocol_zh: 120一分钟识别与避坑：曾去过晋豫陕等山区或西北荒漠疫区者，若长期不规则高热、脾脏明显肿大、消瘦贫血伴全血细胞减少，并突然出现高热寒战休克（继发败血症）、鼻腔/牙龈/消化道大量出血或昏迷（并发噬血细胞综合征HLH），立即拨打120送往有传染病或血液重症救治能力的医院！严禁在未排除黑热病前因“发热+血细胞减少”盲目大剂量使用糖皮质激素（会加速原虫疯长致命）；急诊需立即输血/血小板支持、抗细菌感染并尽快启用两性霉素B脂质体。

master.definition_en: Nevus of Ota is an oculodermal melanocytosis more commonly found in Asian and African populations, usually present at birth and characterized by a usually unilateral, bluish gray, patchy, speckled pigmentation (that may progressively enlarge and darken) affecting the skin of the face along the distribution of the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve (periorbital region, temple, forehead, malar area, nose). In 2/3 cases the ipsilateral sclera is affected. Nevus of Ota usually remains stable once adulthood is reached but an increased risk of glaucoma and uveal melanoma may be observed. Extracutaneous lesions may also occur in cornea, retina, tympanum, nasal mucosa, pharynx, palate. Nevus of Ota occurs as solitary conditions but seldom may occur together with the nevus of Ito or nevus spilus.

Visual morbidity due to complications (including cystoid macular edema and choroidal neovascularization) has been reported.

master.definition_en: A rare common cystic lymphatic malformation characterized by a benign cystic lesion composed of dilated lymphatic channels. Microcystic lesions consist of cysts smaller than 1 cm in diameter. They usually present at birth or during the first years of life and most often occur in the head and neck region but may affect any site. Symptoms depend on the location and extent of the lesion. Infection, trauma, or intracystic hemorrhage can lead to lesional expansion. Malignant transformation does not occur.

master.definition_en: Bobble-head doll syndrome (BHDS) is a rare neurological condition thatis typically first seen in childhood. The signs and symptoms of BHDS includecharacteristic up and downhead movements that increase during walking and excitement and decrease during concentration.Although the specific cause of this condition is unknown, BHDS is often seen with cysts in the third ventricle of the brain that alsocause hydrocephalus (water on the brain). Treatment for BHDS may involve surgical removal of the cyst causing the condition or using a shunt to drain excess water on the brain.
